column3: NKJV has “I must work,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “We must work.”
NKJV has “anointed the eyes of the blind man,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “anointed his eyes.”
NKJV has “that he was blind,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “that he was a beggar.”
NKJV has “He is like him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “No, but he is like him.”
NKJV has “A Man called Jesus” and “Go to the pool of Siloam,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “The man called Jesus” and “Go to Siloam.”
NKJV has “when Jesus made the clay,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “on the day when Jesus made the clay.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV adds “or not.”
